---
title: "Preface"
---

A personal math wiki. One concept per day, 30–60 minutes, written by hand first and then transferred to a `.qmd` file here.

## Goal

Build measure-theoretic probability fluency the long way around: linear algebra fluency first (Axler), then real analysis (Abbott), then probability proper (Rosenthal). Parallel tracks (Needham, Strogatz, Mahajan) keep the geometric and physical instincts alive on lower-energy days.

## Workflow

1. **Session — 30–45 min on paper.** Read the concept. Work an example. Draw the diagram. Write the definition in your own words. The friction is the point.
2. **Transfer — 15–20 min later.** Open a new `.qmd` from `_templates/concept.qmd`. Fill in *Statement → Intuition → Example → Counterexample → Connection to work*. The template surfaces what you don't yet understand.
3. **Photograph the notebook page** and drop it in `notebook/`. Embed alongside the typeset version.

A few hours of delay between handwriting and typing is better than back-to-back — the slight forgetting pressure is useful.

## Cadence

- **Mon–Thu** — primary text, one concept per day
- **Fri** — Needham (or another parallel track)
- **Sat** — synthesis note for the week
- **Sun** — off

See [Schedule](schedule.qmd) for the 24-week plan and [each phase](linear-algebra/index.qmd) for the concept list.

## Repo layout

```
math-notes/
├── _quarto.yml

├── linear-algebra/         # Phase 1 — Axler
├── real-analysis/          # Phase 2 — Abbott
├── measure-theory/         # Phase 3 — Rosenthal
├── complex-analysis/       # Parallel — Needham
├── nonlinear-dynamics/     # Parallel — Strogatz
├── estimation/             # Parallel — Mahajan

```

Render locally with `quarto preview`.
